chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), who said:

Indeed, Allah sent Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) to the jinn and humankind, and after him He appointed twelve successors. Among them are those who passed before, and among them are those who remained; and with every successor a sunnah proceeded. The successors after Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) are upon the sunnah of the successors of Isa, and they were twelve, and Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) was upon the sunnah of al-Masih.

key_terms.أَوْصِيَاءِ: the successors or legatees, specifically those after prophets
key_terms.اللَّهَ: Allah, the One who sends the Prophet and appoints the successors
key_terms.الْإِنْسِ: humankind, the human community addressed by the Prophet’s mission
key_terms.الْجِنِّ: the jinn, one of the two communities addressed by the Prophet’s mission
key_terms.الْمَسِيحِ: the Messiah, Isa, whose pattern is invoked in relation to Amir al-Mu'minin
key_terms.سُنَّةِ: an established divine pattern or way associated with each successor
key_terms.مُحَمَّدًا: Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), the Messenger sent to jinn and humankind
key_terms.وَصِيًّا: a successor or legatee appointed after a prophet

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the twelve successors after Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah sent Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) to both jinn and humankind and appointed twelve successors after him. It links the succession after the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) to a prior divine pattern found in the successors of Isa, presenting the Imamate as part of an established sacred sunnah. It also singles out Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) as being upon the sunnah of al-Masih.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeydullah, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Hamza,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sent Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> to the Jinn and the human and after him<sup>saww</sup> Made twelve succesors<sup>asws</sup>. From them<sup>asws</sup> are some who have preceded, and from them<sup>asws</sup> are some who remain; and every successor<sup>asws</sup>, a Sunnah flowed with him<sup>asws</sup>; and the successors<sup>asws</sup>, those from after Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> are upon the Sunnah of the successors<sup>as</sup> of Isa<sup>as</sup>, they were twelve, and it was so that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was upon the Sunnah of Isa<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl from abu Hamza from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following “

Allah sent Muhammad (s.a.) to all Jinn and manand appointed twelve executors of the will Of these people are those who have left this world and there are those who will have to complete their task. All the executors of the wills (of the prophets) experience certain traditions, Sunnah. The executors of the will after Muhammad (s.a.) experienced the traditions, Sunnah of the executor of the will of Jesus who were twelve in number. Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) experienced the tradition of Jesus.”
